I set my tray down at the end of the table next to Amy and listen in to the current conversation.

"Can we not?" Dean asks tiredly as he looks to Chris.

"Just saying." He puts his hands up and goes back to his food.

"What'd I miss?" I ask Amy.

"Something something Dean wants to move out of state." She says as she pokes her mashed potatoes.

"Not even close." Dean looks over with a look of disbelief.

"That's what I heard." Amy shrugs and takes a bite of her food.

"That's some wild selective hearing." Dennis says from besides Chris.

Amy shrugs.

"Nothing." Dennis tries to get a response. "No snark or sass?"

"Nnnope." She says as she digs into her food.

"Guys I think Amy's broken." Dennis says with a serious face. "Or… fixed?"

"Where's Vicky?" I ask as I look around the cafeteria, not seeing the blonde anywhere.

"Don't know." Dean says, poking at his green beans. "She was supposed to be here by now, but I'm thinking she got caught up in the halls."

"Just going to ignore me?" Dennis says. "Yeah that's okay. I'm used to it. Just let me rot you heartless bastards." He fake sniffles.

"Do it over there." Amy makes a shooing motion with her fork. "Don't need your stench getting any worse."

I flinch as Dennis slaps the table and claps.

"There she is!" He points at Amy victoriously. "Knew the queen of snark was in there."

"If that name sticks." Amy points her fork at Dennis. "I will make you bald."

"And give him a soul?" Chris says, earning an awkward look from everyone else at the table. "Because, he won't be a red head then? And… you know the whole joke… with redheads?"

'Just stop.' I want to say out loud, but don't feel like I can. Not as Missy anyway.

"This is why I'm the funny one." Dennis leans over and whispers loudly.

"You try." Amy says with a comforting tone. "And that's all we can ask, is for you to stop."

If Amy wasn't firmly batting for the other team, I could totally see her and Dennis be a thing.

"Vicky!" Dean says loudly as I look over and see said Dallon sit between Dean and Amy. Vicky's friends Chelsea and Rachel taking seats on the other end of the table. "We were just talking about you."

Vicky looks… like a mix of frustrated and tired as she sets her tray down.

"Whatever it is, Kitsu did it." Vicky says.

"And you say she's not family." Rachel says with a roll of her brown eyes.

"Okay Rache, you're on my last nerve." Vicky says.

'Is everyone in a bad mood today?' I look between Dean, Amy and Vicky. 'What happened?'

"I'm just saying that." She pauses as she looks to me. "Never mind."

'Huh?' I squint my eyes in suspicion. 'What was that about?'

"Stay out of it Rachel." Chelsea grumbles as she pokes her green beans. "It's not our business."

"She deserves to know." I think Rachel says back to her in a quieter but equally harsh whisper.

"What is-"

"It's nothing." Vicky quickly interrupts and looks to me with a forced smile. "What's up new girl?"

"Oh, um… I was just wondering what was going on with you going to Hawaii?" I ask.

"What the hell?" Chelsea asks. "You're going to Hawaii?"

"Am I invited?" Dennis pipes up while Dean leans over and whispers something with Vicky.

"Missy, who told you I was going to Hawaii?" Vicky asks with a strained smile as she leans forward.

"Um, K-Kitsu?" I say, realizing where I might have messed up. "I uh, I overheard her talking about Hawaii in the hall is all. Was uh, I, am I wrong?"

"I fucking called it!" Rachel suddenly announces. Throwing her utensils onto her tray. Leaning forward and pointing an angry finger at Vicky. "I told you!"

"And I'm telling you to drop it!" Vicky shouts back. "Because it's not true!"

"So Kitsu is just casually talking to herself about taking a vacation and only Missy heard it?" Rachel says.

"YES!" Vicky throws her hands up. "She's weird! She does weird things all the time! She poses in front of the mirror and talks to herself she's so weird."

'Is that weird?' I think to all the times I hype myself up in the mirror before a date. 'Wait no, not important. Why do I feel like I'm missing something important?'

"Dean I'd take a strong look at who you're dating." Rachel's face scrunches up with an annoyed smile as she gathers her stuff. "Because someone clearly doesn't care for loyalty!" She gives me a glare.

"What did I do?" I ask while returning the glare.

"Don't act so innocent." She gives me a dirty look. "Or do you want to explain what you were doing? You know what? No, you know and should be ashamed of yourself. Think of how Vista will feel once she finds out."

"Pfft!" Amy spews out her food.

"W-whay Iyai, what do you mean?" I stutter out.

"Coming!" Dennis suddenly gets up with his tray and leaves.

"I should uh, I should go." Chris also gets up. "He's my ride, you understand."

"Plausible deniability." Chelsea suddenly gets up.

"Huh?" My heart thuds as I look around, confused at the rapid course of events that just went down.

Rachel just rolls her eyes and leaves. Leaving me, Amy, Dean and Vicky on one side of the table.

"Sup nerds." Carlos says as he sits down across from Dean. "What'd I miss?"

I wish I knew!

-4 hours later-

"I'm all packed!" I run into the kitchen and announce as I hold my suitcase above my head.

Mom and Dad look at me as I enter. Taking in all my glorious cuteness as I stand before them. Dad pausing his stirring of a pot, and mom stopping her daily intake of sustenance.

Mom and Dad look between each other. Their eyes giving off an air of concerned parent mixed with annoyed parent.

I'll let you guess who's who.

"What? No." I tilt my head in confusion. "It's Tuesday."

"Next Tuesday." Dad says and points to my suitcase. "And is that my suitcase?"

"No." I say and turn to Mom. "This Tuesday."

"Why is that a defining point?" She challenges. "The tickets are for next Tuesday."

"The only foot with an issue is bout to be mine when I kick your butt." He says seriously. "Now seriously, put that back where you found it. It was a wedding gift from my father."

"Oh." I concede as I look down to the black case. "Oops."

Carol "Brandish" Dallon POV

Then there's the "trip" to Hawaii. If you can call being bribed to investigate the disappearance of a Ward as a vacation. And that's not including the fact that I have to handle all the paperwork of said vacation for my work.

And that's not even including the fact that The Marquis is still out there. And potentially all of the Birdcage.

"You alright, honey?" Mark asks and I look up to him. Recalling the way I saw him in that storage container. Wires and tubes flowing through his open chest and limbs. Looking like a set piece for Hellraiser.

"Carol?" He looks over to me as he sets the lid on the pot.

I get up and walk over to him. Ignoring his concerned look as I wrap my arms around him and lay my head on his chest.

"I get it." He says. "A lot has happened and you've had so much to deal with."

"I don't fucking know." I hiss. "Last time I thought I had her figure out she brought the dead back to life. Then turned them into furry."

"Hey, I'm the smart one." I glare up at him.

"I know, it's why you married me." He smirks, making me feel twenty years younger. "A loving man who can appreciate you in every way." He gives me a comfortable squeeze that really makes me feel like I'm in my teens.

"Hey, no!" I bring a finger up to dissuade his obvious intentions. "… Save it for the hotel room." I say quietly.

"Gladly." He says and pulls me back in for a kiss.

And my mother said we'd be divorced in five years. Good thing I never listened to her.

"Oh come on, you've felt it way more." Mark rolls his eyes.

"Not that!" I swat his shoulder. "I just, had a realization."

"What kind?" He asks as I feel the it go down and stop poking my thigh.

"Am I raising the girls to be just like me?" I ask.

"What?" He asks.

"Am I turning into my mother?" I rephrase.

Mark pauses. His body going stiff in other ways than one a moment before.

"Huh!?" He says loudly. "Coming!" He lets go and steps away from me.

"What, I didn't hear anything. Mark!" I call after him.

"Sorry honey, someone's at the door!" He says, now jogging out of the kitchen.

"Mark!"

Krrrrr

"I didn't do it!" Kitsu shouts from her room upstairs.

"She's getting to that point again, Francis." Oliver says as soon as I walk into the hideout.

Because I just love bad news right out the gate.

"Jesus Christ Ollie." I groan as I take my mask off and rub my face. "I just got here, give a man a moment to decompress. Shit."

I reach into my pocket and go for a pack. I sigh to myself, noticing I only have one cigarette left. Setting the cigarette in my mouth and crumpling the now empty pack. Shoving it in my pocket for later as I head to my bug out bag and grab another.

"Francis, I'm sorry I-I can't keep doing this." Oliver starts stuttering nervously as I pocket the fresh pack. Turning to him as I light the cancer stick in my mouth. "I, she, if it were just the mutations and the growths… it'd be fine. I'd be fine! I would. But, the way she looks at me sometimes anymore. Like she doesn't recognize me unless I'm talking."

"Oliver." I pause to let out a breath of smoke. Keeping my gaze level with the eternally shifting man. "You literally change your face with the weather. I mean for fuck's sake your eyes are turning blue as we speak."

He was Asian when he got into K-Pop for a bit. That was weird to adjust to. Not that him being Asian was bad thing. But Oliver is one bout of gender dysphoria away from being a playboy model I swear.

"You know what I mean." He levels a flat stare. "She looks at me like, like I'm a piece of meat."

"Hey, that's still my girlfriend you're talking about." I point my cigarette at him and playfully warn him. "Don't go accusing her of-"

"God dammit Francis!" Oliver yells in my face, shocking me by smacking my cigarette out of my hand. "I'm being serious here!"

He huffs, clearly having forced that out of himself. His face red with anger, but his expression is one of worry. Fear, even. While mine is no doubt one of shock as we stare at each other.

"Please." Oliver says shakily. "I know… you're just trying to deflect. To pretend everything is alright a-and to make everything seem okay. But it's not. Not anymore."

He looks like he wants to say more. But his mouth moves soundlessly as he just, can't seem to get the words out. Or rather he just won't. For whatever reason, deciding not to continue.

"Okay." I swallow the spit that had been pooling in my mouth. "I'll, talk to her. See how it's going."

"That's all I'm really asking." Oliver lets go of a breath he was holding in. His shoulders going slack in relief.

Not that there's anything to really be relieved about.

Me and Oliver stare awkwardly at each other for a bit. Neither of us really wanting to be the first to move. But, nothing'll get done so I step around him. Wordlessly heading further into the abandoned subway. Further away from the rest of the group than we initially had been.

'How bad can it get this time?' I ask myself. My chest growing tight in anticipation of meeting with Noelle. The only answer I get being the echo of my footsteps on the hard concrete ground. Passing our original camp we set up.

Before Noelle hit her most recent spiral. Scaring the others into moving further in and closer to the emergency bug out exit.

Tang!

I eventually steel myself to keep going further down the old dark tunnel. Finding Noelle's room. I feel the pressure of anxiety grow in my head as I want nothing more than to leave and lay down. Let the day pass, go to bed and wake up to a better day.

"Just do it you coward." I tell myself as I reach for the metal door, turning the safe like wheel on the front of the entrance. Forcing the door open, eliciting a squeak from the rusty hinges.

And through the dark, I lay my eyes on the horrid monstrosity of flesh that once was Noelle. No, it still is Noelle. It's just, mostly something else. Something evil and ugly that's taken up space. Like a cancer made into a fucked up power.

"The one and only." I push off the doorframe and hold my hands out. Giving her a little twirl to show myself off, and finishing with a bow.

"Heehehe." She chuckles over the sound of grumbling and gravel shifting under her immense weight. "You haven't been here in a while."

"That's not true." I shake my head slightly. "We talked just yesterday, remember?"

"No we didn't." She calls my bluff, her stomach growling and causing her to wince under the pangs of hunger.

"You lie to me all the time." She says darkly, her voice taking an unnatural edge.

"Only the best of lies." I wink, making her pause and blink as she tries to figure out what I mean.

"I suppose that's true." She says softly as she visibly relaxes and leans forward on her own mound of flesh. "So, what's been going on? You guys don't really tell Ollie anything, and so I don't really know anything."

'That's because we don't want you knowing how up shit's creek we are.' I grimace on the inside.

"To be fair, he never asks." I hold a hand up in my defense. "So if you're gonna chew anyone out for that, save it for him."

I realize my mistake as soon as the words leave my mouth. The mention of chewing having a chain reaction on Noelle's lower half that makes its influence clear as her face darkens. The rumbling hunger cutting through the sound of my own blood pumping in my ears.

"What have you been doing, Francis?" She asks softly. The light leaving her eyes unreflective and soulless as they look through me.

"What do you mean?" I ask with a forced smile. "I've been-"

"Why haven't you done anything?" Noelle cuts me off with her tone monotonous and eerily lacking an echo in this room.

A room she is out growing. When we got here, she was the size of small a van. Now she's nearly the size of a bus. She's getting worse.

And she's getting worse faster.

"I've been working on a few things Noelle." I say as I pull out a cigarette. Only to freeze as the pack is knocked out of my hand before I can finish opening it.

"Y-you know how I hate those things Francis." She says in a shaky voice as a tear trails down her face.

My breath catches in my throat as she moves closer to me. Her body rumbling and squelching as she leans forward. Looking down on me with a face twisted in concern. Eyes clearly red from crying and hair matted from not being kept.

The others are too scared to go near her anymore. Even Oliver won't stay near for too long. And I see why.

No, I already knew why.

"Those things are killing you." She says softly as she reaches out and caresses my cheek. "I… I don't want you hurting yourself like that for me. Not when it hurts you so much."

Her face trembles, the edges of her lips twitching into a shaky smile as she lets out a small laugh. It's a good thing I freeze when I'm scared. Because there's no telling how she'd act if I'd flinched or yelped.

"You always know how to cheer me up Krouse." She says. "Remember the trip to starbucks?"

We never went to a starbucks together.

"The one where we were banned from ever returning?" I chuckle, regaining some nerve to keep myself here as I keep her placated. "Yeah… in my defense that barista was putting on a few pounds."

"Hahahah!" She snorts and giggles, her body writhing under her in some odd facsimile of excitement as she pulls back and covers her mouth. "She was being a total bitch!"

"Yeah, she kinda had it coming." I chuckle with her as I take a step back towards the door. Only for a fucking eye to open up on her lower half, centering right on me and dilating with focus.

'Well fuck me if that isn't new!' I keep my panic to myself.

"She did." Noelle giggles as she covers her face with both hands and laughs. "You really showed her in World of Warcraft. Beat her real good."

Again, that never happened.

"Those were good times." She says as her arms go slack. Her lower half rumbling. "Why haven't we played any games Francis?"

"Well, we've just had trouble getting an ethernet cable down here. Can't really use wifi in-"

"In a cave? In a sewer?" She mutters as tendrils grow up and towards her. "In the dark, always in the dark you don't tell me anything!" She leans forward and screams at me, several mouths screaming in tandem with her as she loses herself. Tendrils shooting up from her waste and covering her in a protective case.

And I book it out of there. Slamming the metallic door and sealing it shut as she slams herself against it. Loud gongs and cracks pass my ears as I seal it and take off. Not trusting the door to hold her for even a minute as I run into the main area where the others are waiting.

"Francis, what's going-" Oliver starts to ask from his seat on a foldable chair.

"Code black! Move!" I shout as I pass the blonde man, slowing down to get a hand under his armpit and force him up. "Go! Go!" I rush towards Jess and pull her out of her wheelchair.

"Ah!" She squeaks as I turn with her in my arms and run while Marissa runs ahead with Oliver, both grabbing the bug out bags. "Already!?"

"Yep!" I grunt as I keep her in a princess carry, my straining under her weight.

This was normally Luke's job. But well, that bastard walked out on us!

"Throw me over your shoulder!" Jess yells over the sound of the collapsing subway tunnels. "It'll be easier for you that way!"

"Augh you're shoulders are so boney." She groans.

"Yeah, sorry but I haven't had time to get in my shoulder presses so you'll have to deal." I huff as I try to catch up with Oliver and Marissa.

"Aaaaaauuuuggghh!" Noelle screams an ungodly and horrific sound that's somewhere between a wolf's howl and an elk's screech. And the tunnels behind us shake before collapsing. Cutting her away from us as we flee her rampage.

'This is your fault.' I feel water run down my face as my throat tightens. 'You failed her. You always fail her.'

As the sounds of rubble and screams fade behind me. I can't help but try to ignore my lead feet as I run. Oliver and Marissa already far ahead of me and getting further out of sight. Not bothering to look back and make sure I'm following.

Why would they?

Blinded by having his eyes pulverized, Blastzone lashes out. Gathering energy in his chest and launching blast after blast in random directions. Only the sound of rubble and explosions reaching his ears as he panics and desperately tries to keep any threats at bay. Before he's stopped in his tracks. A sickening squelch cutting through the sound of his own tantrum, and he reaches down. Feeling his hot blood coat his hands as he grips a pole.

Several yards away, Armsmaster had gotten to a secure vantage point in an apartment building and thrown his halberd in its javelin form. Hitting Blastzone inbetween the muscles of his abs, before recalling it back to his hand with its teleporting feature. Leaving a gaping wound in the clone's gut.

Armsmaster collapses the weapon and holsters it to his back, turning tail and runs into the building's hallway as Blastzone's creator turns its attention on him. He didn't need to see it to know it was chasing him. The sounds of the building he was in steadily collapsing behind him was informative enough.

"Time to give this a shot." He mutters to himself as he activates his suit's newly installed overhaul mode. Inspired by the Blue Blur of Brockton Bay. All power being rerouted to his armor shielding and hydraulics, he charges fast enough to match a low tier speedster as he reaches the end of the hall. Bursting through the wall at the end of the hall, leaping out of the fifth story of the building with the monster crashing through right behind him.

A limp stretches out and goes to swipe Armsmaster, nearly getting him before he's caught. Swept up by an allied flyer. His wings beating harshly to flee the monster and keep Armsmaster safe.

"Fuck you're heavy!" Firebreather curses as he flies a block over, putting two buildings out of sight between them and the monster. Where once a safe distance away, he unceremoniously drops Armsmaster before gracelessly crashing himself.

Armsmaster looks up to his rescuer, and takes in his disheveled state as Firebreather shakily gets to his hands and knees. His left wing torn and bloody, the muscles of his shoulder and left arm exposed to the open air.

"Go home, kid." Armsmaster says. "Or at least sit out until you're healed up."

"Like fucking hell." Fire glares at the experienced hero. Turning his head to reveal the broken horns and missing eye on his left side as the harrowed man stubbornly gets to his feet.

"You're running on pure adrenaline." Armsmaster warns as he turns away from the orange man. "The moment that wears out you're likely to die."

But Firebreather was not listening, and had already taken off back towards the fight.

Back on the main street, the monster known as Noelle was in a full charge. Cutting through a building and devouring people in her path. The monstrosity of various animals forming on it to better help it devour and tear through the building. From a shark head taking place of the wolf, stretching out and snatching victims. Swallowing them whole or cleaving through their bodies. To a malformed and overly muscled giraffe head swinging around on a long neck, its horns acting as a sledge hammer to knock down structures and pulverize the fleeing civilians.

A young man is running, nearly tripping over his own legs in his panic when the horns of the giraffe make contact with his side… and in a blur he appears in a parking lot. Then a woman appears next to him. Then a child, and another man. Soon, people are piling into the lot, all being escorted by a flash of blue light.

Reginald "A-Train" Franklin POV

.

"Whew!" I come to a stop at the end of the street. Watching the chimera from Hellraiser demo a building and crawl onto the street. Now larger than when it went in. Where it was maybe the size of a bus when I first showed up, now it's a big bus. "Man fuck this city, bro." I can't help but feel my arms and shoulders go slack in sheer, utter exasperation.

I ain't even been up more than an hour! I been done woken up by the sounds of police cars going through my neighborhood a bit ago, and let me tell you. Nothing wakes you up faster than running for dear life.

Having caught my breath. I charge back towards the creature's scene of destruction as the orange lizard dude starts bombarding the thing with waves of fire as it swoops down. Doing barrel rolls to dodge out the way of its freaky limbs.

While I keep out of its way and grabbing the people on the ground. Running them to the parking lot three blocks east and keeping this thing on a diet.

"Shit!" I curse as an arm as long as a streetlamp swipes at me. Forcing me to slide under, across the rough and broken road underneath.

I slide on the limb and roll back to my feet. Picking up my momentum once more as I see a kid being pulled by their arm in one of the thing's many jaws. Tossing the screaming kid up like a piece of popcorn.

Everything happens in slow motion for me as I'm unable to reach the kid. Before I get an idea. A reckless, and very dumb idea. One I don't even realize I'm doing as I just move.

'Come on, you got this!' I hype myself up as I get closer. 'Can't stop, won't stop, don't stop!'

I hurdle jump over a bit of rubble, planting my foot on a larger bit of debris as I leap up. My heart thudding as my momentum sends me rocketing towards the twenty foot tall monster. Everything happening so fast, yet I'm able to keep everything in focus with vivid detail.

"You can't stop the A-Train!" I roar as my blood becomes pure adrenaline. My feet in front of me as I land on the damn thing's side with a sickening crunch. And I run.

I run right up and across its body, feeling bits of its flesh give way under my feet. It's surface caving under my steps like I'm running on a trampoline. Making it to the lip of the open mouth, I leap off it and towards the boy. Forcing its jaw shut with the force of my jump as I reach out and catch the falling kid midair.

"Wooooo!" I yell through my adrenaline rush as I fall with the boy in my arms. The ground quickly approaching, home run just in sight.

Creak

"Ah!" My eyes bulge in response to the pain in my legs. My knees and ankles popping with the force of my decent as I don't quite stick the landing.

'Can't stop!' I grit my teeth and run on burning shins. My vision pulsing in time with my blood as I run. And I run, I run all the way to the lot I was leaving people in. falling to my knees in an exhausted pain as my legs cry for a break.

"Aaaah!" I let out a cry of pain as needles shoot through legs the moment I stop moving.

"Aaaaaaah! Ahahahahaaaa!" The little boy in my arms screams as I let him go and the sounds of everything return to me in full. And I look down to the boy.

Pale and covered in his blood. His arm held on by a few strands of muscle and ligaments.

"Hey!" I shout to the crowd of people roaring in confusion. "HEY! HEY!" I scream my voice raw. "I NEED A DOCTOR! HELP!"

But my voice doesn't get over the crowd. And the boy stops screaming in my arms.

"Fuck!" I slam my fist into the ground. Letting down the boy, pale and cold. Probably no older than twelve. "I'm sorry. I'm, I can't."

With a scream of frustration I get up. And I run, I run right back to the fight.

Director Emily Piggot POV

"You're telling me you have nothing to do with this." I ask the sociopathic blonde tween bio-tinker. Holding up a tablet with live video feed of the monstrosity going on a killing spree in the western part of the city.

It's disturbing how many of those are in the city. It's disturbing that two even exist. Tween sociopathic bio-tinkers that is.

"Nope!" She says cheerfully from her place in the cell, restrained by a straight jacket and stuck in a chair. "Though I kinda wish I did. I mean, how do you even get that many heads to work on a body and have it still move? They have to be empty inside. Or the brain of the creature is compartmentalized similar to an orca's and only one task is ever focused at a time. But even then-"

"Just keep her talking." Head researcher Jamez says next to me, just out of sight of the serial killer. "Even if she didn't make it, her insight might prove something invaluable."

"-But that's just a theory. I little guessy-guess." She giggles. And then looks directly at me, and stops. "You don't get it."

"I don't." I admit.

"Watch a movie once in a while. Jeez you're no fun." She puffs out her cheeks. "When do I get to meet with sissy, or talk to Mr. Jack?"

"Jack Slash is still on the run." I lie to her. "And Kitsu has yet to reach out to you, and we've had a lot on our plates. Like now."

It's a delaying tactic, I know. We can't very well admit that Jack Slash was found dead in an alley somewhere in the slums, and I'll swallow the barrel of a gun before I allow Kitsu to meet with Bonesaw.

For one, I don't think I could get her to do so. For two, I can guarantee that meeting won't end well.

"I'm bored!" Bonesaw yells out.

"I'm sorry to hear that." I say as I go to another angle of the live feed. Which immediately catches her attention like jingling keys.

"Ooh! Is that, huh." She tilts her head and tries to lean forward. "Bring that closer."

"You can see it from here." I say from the interrogation window where I'm not even five feet from her.

"Then zoom in! Jeez you can't even think to- augh!" She puffs out her cheeks, before sighing. "I'm sorry, that was rude. Can you please zoom in on the top of the image?"

Everyday her moodswings get more frequent. She claims it's because she doesn't have access to her equipment. But I can't very well trust her word on that.

Regardless, I do so. And zoom in on the image. Watching as she leans forward as much as she can, squinting her eyes to get a better look. A moment later her mismatching eyes go wide in recognition and she trembles in her restraints.

"Ooh! Ooh!" She almost bounces in her seat. "You have to let me out, like, right now now."

"And why would I ever do that?" I scrutinize the eternal twelve year old.

"Because, I know how to handle that creature." She says.

"Then why not tell us." I challenge the serial killer.

"Because then I wouldn't get anything I want?" She rolls her eyes. "I mean, not to sound rude but duh."

The way her and Kitsu speak and act are so disturbingly similar, words will never do justice. The cold, distant eyes that seem to focus on a million things yet nothing at all. And the callous disregard for life in general, like death has no consequence.

And the worst part, is that it doesn't. Not to them. Bonesaw has, on multiple occasions, resurrected the dead into some twisted facsimile of life. And the living proof of Kitsu's inability to comprehend mortality is living on the base.

"Anything you'd say in regards on how to stop it?" I ask.

"Nope!" She says with a smile. "Not unless I can get a strawberry smoothie."

Exact, fucking same. They are the same person.

"We'll see about that." I say as I remove the tablet from the window.

"And not the cruddy ones from the cafeteria here!" She says as I stand up. "I want one from McDonalds."

"We're done here." I say as I walk away from the interrogation window.

"You know my-" Her voice is cut off by the blast shield shutting.

Personally, I'd have gassed the room and ended her. But we don't know what all she has going on inside her. And I've been "gently informed" that turning her into an asset should be a priority.

"Ma'am." Head Researcher Jamez says as he keeps pace with me. "Looking over the creature, it's clear it has biomorphing capabilities. I understand prioritizing evacuation but why are we not calling in a possible Endbringer threat?"

"Because an Endbringer level threat implies that we are entirely incapable of handling the situation and that the entirety of the PRT's resources are insufficient."

"But our resources here are insufficient." The dark skinned man says. "I understand not calling in Kitsu, two bioshifters in one spot is… not ideal. But you're actively holding back and not-"

"If I pull teams from the slums, the Merchants and Teeth will destroy the place. If I pull anyone from the south then the ABB are likely to reestablish footholds in the warehouses." I explain. "And that's not even counting the remnants of the Empire and the vacuum that's still in place and only being held off by the presence of one little girl in the city."

"And that very same little girl is easily bribed into-"

"Jamez." I turn to the man with a stern glare. Silencing the parahuman obsessed man. "I will not risk our safety net for something unless we need it."

"Safety net?" He raises a brow.

Brockton Bay, is one of the top ten cities at risk for an Endbringer attack in the next ten years. And I have no interest of removing either of our Endstoppers if I have to. Lung maybe, but only if he forced the situation.

"In case of a real threat." I say cautiously. "And that's all I'll say on the matter."

"Real threat, what could be a bigger threat than- no." Jamez figures out what I mean.

"Go back to your lab, Jamez." I order him, not entertaining this conversation any further. "If things are getting desperate, we'll call her."

I only hope this doesn't get to that point. But the practical part of me knows we're one PRT casualty from running out of excuses.

A/N Into The Black Mirror

Alt title: Self Reflection

Heads up, this chapter is almost entirely in 3rd person POV and switches a lot. There's no way I can do first person POV and not make it confusing as hell. There's just too much to tell.

.

GideonBlackthorn: Kitsu could honestly go either way. It genuinely depends on her mood.

If she's in a neutral or good mood, she'd likely to recognize that Noelle is not in control. And will help her. If she's in a poor mood, she's not even likely to try.

RadChaos897: The problem with the Game Theory quote, is that Bonesaw was going to be the one to make the reference. Not Kitsu. If it was Kitsu, I would've just gone "fuck it" and put it in.

I hope you like the experiment in third person POV.

Grimnosh: Your theory and more will be proven in this chapter but with Piggot? She's really in a 'damned if you do damned if you don't' situation. Kitsu could kill Noelle with little difficulty. But the risk of a Kitsu clone is simply just not something Piggot is willing to risk. She'd rather call in the Wards and the Triumvirate than risk THAT!

Gogmazios: You're welcome!

-West Slums, Tuesday, October 19th, 1:19am-

Francis "Trickster" Krouse POV

.

'Fuck fuck fuck, fuck!' I freak out in the privacy of my own mind as I look upon the scene of ongoing destruction. 'This is too much. She's going too far!'

Her previous rampages all ended within minutes of them starting. But this one has been going on half an hour. And she's showing no sign of stopping soon.

'Is it the location?' I ask myself. 'We always made sure to move her to places she can't do much harm. Is it the, oh god.'

I realize the mistake we made in staying here too long. We'd usually move by now, or at least head to a less populated area for Noelle. Could the, could her feeding be the cause of this? The extended rampage.

'I really thought we'd have more time.' I think as I bite my nail. 'Or hopefully have this solved by now.'

"What to do?" I say under my breath, my words barely reaching my ears over the sound of Noelle's rampage.

"What do we do, Francis?" Marissa asks from behind me. Snapping me from my thoughts. "We… we can't just wait this one out like the others."

'I don't think waiting will do anything.' I think to myself as I swallow my nerves. 'At this rate, she'll just keep going and going.'

"Why not?" Oliver asks softly as I turn around. His arms crossed over his chest as he regards the dancer. "I mean, what can we do?"

A small, very small intrusive thought tells me to run. That we can cut our loses and pretend we know nothing.

I shoot that thought with a shotgun.

"People are actively dying you idiot!" Jess hisses from her seat against an AC unit. "And it's mostly our fault."

"No it's not!" Oliver stomps his foot. "And I'm not going to pretend that it is anymore!"

"Oliver, what do you-" I start to ask.

"Look at me guys." He puts his hands on his chest as he starts to slowly grow buffer. "What can I do? You, you can't possibly expect me to face off against, against that!" His voice cracks as he points to the sounds of destruction in the distance.

"She has a name Oliver! Use it!" I snap at the cowardly blonde. The man flinches back, despite his figure now being a head taller than me. He's still the shy and cowardly Oliver we all know. "Jess, can you make something that can restrain her?" I turn my attention away from the pansy and to the more useful members of our group.

'That's not fair and you know it.' I admonish myself.

"Huh?" She jolts in surprise. "Um, yeah I can think of something."

"Good, Mars." I turn to the only other fielder left in our dysfunctional little family. "I'm going to need a few suns from you. I have a plan to restrain Noelle, but you'll need to be a bit more, spicy with your powers."

I give her my usual smile. Keeping up an image of stability to keep us together.

"Alright." She says with a tight jaw. "But, Francis, what if this plan doesn't-"

"We'll deal with that when we get to it." I say as I take out a pack, only for my hands to shake as my fingers fish around inside an empty pocket.

Putting both hands into my pockets to play off the move as intentional. I turn around and face the city, in the direction of Noelle's rampage. My teeth grinding as I feel a sense of irritation wash over me.

"I have a plan guys." I say calmly as I look over my shoulder and give them a smile. "Trust me, alright? I've gotten us through worse haven't I?"

How I wish that line was true. By everything fucked and holy do I wish it were. But you know what they say, fake it till you make it.

3rd person POV

.

Firebreather continues to swoop down and unleash streams of flame onto the monster's various heads. Using his superior flight skills to dodge and weave around limbs and appendages that reach out and swipe at him.

"Shit!" He curses as the wind bites at his exposes muscle. Holding back the urge to wince and slow down as he buys time for Lady Photon to get help. And hopefully return with backup.

'Just a little longer.' He thinks to himself. 'One more minute, you can do this!'

He focuses on the pain, allowing it to keep him focused through the chaos as he makes a sharp turn up. Dodging an exoskeletal limb that reaches for him, like a giant elongated roach's leg. He doesn't bother to blast any flames at it, knowing it's useless against the armored sections.

Firebreather reaches the height of the nearby buildings. Well above what the creature is currently capable of reaching. But even he knows that's a 'for now' statement as the creature steadily grows with every innocent civilian it consumes.

Pheeeeeeew

Firebreather instinctively closes his wings. His flight training with Crystal and Sarah kicking in. Telling him how to best dodge the incoming projectile. Just in time to see the green orb shoot past above his head.

"Ack!" He coughs up spit under the force of an armored fist slamming into his back. A sickening crack reaching his ears as his back pops under the strength of the punch.

Before he can register what's happening. The assailant grabs his sinew exposed shoulder and digs his claws in, making Fire hiss in pain as he's tossed back onto a nearby roof. A piece of his shoulder being ripped out in the process.

Firebreather slams into the hard surface of the roof with a loud crack. The roof beneath him fracturing and cracking beneath him.

Blastzone doesn't give his blueprint time to recover. Dropping down and slamming a foot into his chest, further compromising the stability of the structure beneath them as Fire has the wind knocked out of him. Now coughing up a bit of blood.

"You know, I shouldn't be surprised you survived that blast." Blastzone huffs as he keeps one bloodied eye close and a hand held over his abdomen. "I am based off of you. It'd be rather pathetic if you kicked the can that quickly."

Fire spits out a bit of blood pooling in his mouth. Glaring at his clone and grabbing his ankle.

"You talk too much." Firebreather spits out, using what little strength he has left to try and force him off.

"I suppose I do." His copy grins menacingly. His snaking out and wrapping around Firebreather's neck. The long, muscular appendage tightening around his neck, cutting off blood to his head and air to his lungs.

Firebreather struggles as his consciousness starts to fade. The last thing he wants see, being the warped image of himself grinning down at him as he opens his bloody eye. Revealing the freshly healed organ.

.

.

Armsmaster looks over to the scuffle between the two reptilian Case 53's. His mind weighing the odds of a direct fight, and determining it to be against his best interests. He had warned Firebreather, and it's not as though the New Wave cape is his responsibility.

So with that thought in mind, Armsmaster looks down to the rampaging monstrosity below. His HUD picking up the highspeed activity of Brockton's premier independent hero, A-Train, as the man rescues as many people as possible. Somehow avoiding the creature's notice, or simply moving too fast for it to truly respond as the blue blur makes off with its meals.

Taking advantage of the beast's distracted state and his own altitude advantage. Armsmaster takes out his halberd and-

"Collin!" Dragon's voice echoes through his HUD. Briefly making the armored man pause.

"What?" He asks as he readies his halberd disruptor pulse, the 'blade' of the weapon humming with a soft blue glow that illuminates his surroundings.

"You need to help Firebreather!" She urges him.

"He's helping me." Armsmaster says pointed as he aims.

"Collin there's nothing to suggest a strategic strike will even work, you need to disable Blastzone or he's likely to focus all his attention on-" Armsmaster mutes his HUD's comms. Irritating the smitten AI with his antics.

"Won't know until we try." Armsmaster says under his breath, knowing Dragon can still hear him.

Lining up his shot, Armsmaster throws his weapon. The silvery blue tinkertech blade hums through the air as it arcs towards the monster's front head. Landing true on its temple.

Bwooom

A low warping boom sounds out as an explosion of blue energy knocks the head to the side. The beast roaring out in pain as the upper half of its skull is blown off. Stumbling and slamming into a building. Rubble and glass rain down on the injured creature.

Armsmaster focuses his attention on the creature's entire being as the head slowly reforms, pulling from the mass of its immense body. Shrinking ever so slightly. The eyes of the monstor all turn, honing in on Armsmaster's position as his halberd teleports back into his hand.

The multiple heads of the monster open their maws. And a moment later unleash a horrific screech that rings Armsmaster's ears even through his built in protections.

"Collin! What the rrrrmmm! You're so stubborn!" Dragon manages to bypass his settings and unmute herself. "Good job! My nearest suit is still a minute out and here you are… what did that even accomplish?"

"Valuable information." He says as he starts running, activating the newly installed overhaul mode to speed away and jump off the other side of the building. "We now know damaging it reduces its mass. It obeys the laws of conservation."

"Anyone could've guessed that. Collin you're just being stubborn and hardheaded." Dragon says after calming herself down. "You're doing what you want, and justifying it after the fact."

Armsmaster says nothing as he lands in an alley and takes off. Dodging around the sharp turns of the backstreets to evade the monster's detection as it mindlessly charges the building he was on. Running to find a new vantage point from where he can try and find its weak point.

Meanwhile, the roaring screech of the monster reaches Blastzone's ears, gaining his attention like a commander's call. Making him turn his attention to the tinker that had just done great harm to his creator. Snarling, Blastzone's eyes hone in on the figure just as he retrieves his weapon and turns tail to escape his creator's wrath.

"Cheap shotting bastard." Blastzone hisses.

But his focused anger is short lived as Firebreather takes advantage of Blastzone's distraction to surprise the clone. Letting go of the ankle planted on his chest and elbowing the roof beneath him. Collapsing the already damaged concrete and sending them both down into the building as Firebreather takes the advantage and rips Blastzone's tail from his neck. Just as they fall into the apartment of a cowering family.

-West Slums, Tuesday, October 19th, 1:30am-

.

.

3rd Person POV, with Trickster and Ballistic

.

Ballistic ducks behind the counter of the fabric store as Trickster disappears from his sight. Their fight taking them inside a nearby building as Trickster kited Ballistic, effectively forcing him into the structure.

"It doesn't have to go like this!" Trickster's voice echoes throughout the shop.

Ballistic knows he fucked up. Francis may not have been a good leader, or even a pleasant one. But he always excelled at tactical maneuvers.

And he just let himself be cornered.

"You're right!" Ballistic shouts back, crouching low and keeping below the countertop. "Just step away Francis!"

"No real names." He hears the man's voice in his ear before an arm finds its way around his neck.

"Gack!" Ballistic chokes as Trickster throws him back.

Ballistic grabs a ball bearing from his pocket and aims it at Trickster's hip. Firing it in time to hit a display mannequin. Blasting bits of plastic as Ballistic gets up and runs for the backrooms.

"Just walk away Ballistic!" Ballistic hears from the main floor of the shop as he finds the door to the backrooms and looks for the stairs. "We don't have to fight!"

"You're right!" He shouts back. "Just step away Francis!"

Ballistic bursts the back door and enters the stairwell. Running up the first flight he turns to the second floor landing, seeing his old teammate. He pauses, waiting for him do something.

"You know I can't do that." The teleporter says solemnly, letting slip the mask he put up. "You know, I can't let you take her life."

Trickster's chest trembles under his vest. As though holding back something he desperately wants to say.

"You can, just do nothing." Ballistic, otherwise known as Luke, says with a firm voice.

"Now where's the fun in that?" Trickster leans to one side, hand on his hip as he points up. "When I went through the trouble of setting up the perfect playground!"

Following his direction, Ballistic looks up the stairwell. And feels his eyes go wide as he sees a series of corner mirrors and mannequins on the landings and stairs.

Trickster's teleportation works based on sight, and mass. With mannequins that almost perfect take up the same volume, if the mannequins are weighted, and Ballistic knows they are. It wouldn't even take a second for Trickster to swap with them.

"The top floor of this place is storage. Who knew a fabric store would have so many mannequins?" Trickster explains with an air of superiority. "Still want to do this, Luke?"

Luke looks to the mocking visage of Trickster's mask. A strange bundle of feelings too complicated for him to understand well up in his gut. An odd mix of annoyance and pity that he hates. Conflicting against a background of apathy. Of not wanting to do this.

"This ends here." Trickster says seriously.

Rather than saying anything, Ballistic grabs a handful of fishing weights from his pocket and aims them up.

"You honestly think you can-"

"Just shut up!" Ballistic yells as he unleashes the projectiles. Buckshotting the stairwell and breaking nearly every visible mirror.

The sound of broken glass makes Trickster instinctively raise his arms to protect his face as shards rain down. A moment of distraction that Ballistic takes to run up the stairs and body check him against the wall.

"Ugg!" Trickster gasps as the wind is knocked from his lungs. Ballistic throws him to the ground and stomps on his face, waiting a moment to make sure he doesn't get up before turning and running up the stairs.

Ballistic makes it to the fourth story before a stabbing pain throbs in his leg. Looking back, he sees Trickster behind him. Bloody knife in hand that had been slipped into the seems of his armor. Hitting a non-vital area of his leg.

"You dick!" Ballistic shouts. "You stabbed me!"

Ballistic moves to punch him and send him tumbling down the staircase. Only for his fist to meet a dusty mannequin, knocking its head off and sending it down.

He turns around, expecting a sneak attack. But not seeing anything.

"And you head kicked me!" Trickster swings from the staircase above him. Nailing him in the side with both feet. Slamming Ballistic into the wall and clumsily landing next to him.

Trickster raises a foot to kick Ballistic down the stairs. But loses his footing as Ballistic grabs his ankle and pulls. Sending the man down, the back of his head hitting the stairs with a sharp clack.

Hissing in pain, Trickster doesn't get to recover as Ballistic crawls on top of him. Whaling into Trickster's masked face. Making use of his heavier frame to keep the thinner man pinned and helpless.

But a moment later, Ballistic finds himself under Trickster as the two switch places. Blinking from the disorientation, Trickster takes the opportunity to look up and spot a mannequin in the reflection of an unbroken mirror. Disappearing just as Ballistic moves to toss him off.

Ballistic gets up, frustrated and losing his patience.

"Why!?" He calls out. "You know what's happening! You know what she's doing!"

"Do you really have to ask?" Trickster's voice echoes through the stairwell. "I'm not just going to let you kill Noelle!"

"That is not Noelle!" Ballistic yells back. "Stop pretending she's still in there! All that's left is a shell of human pretending to be someone you love!"

Ballistic continues to run up the stairs. Keeping an ear out for any changes as he stays on guard. Roughly tossing aside any mannequins he passes to get rid of Trickster's set up. Passing a mannequin that he shoves aside and behind him, he feels a change in weight of the object and spots a flash of color in the corner of his eye.

Turning around, he pulls a small weight from his pocket and throws it. Nailing Trickster in the chest with the force of a professional boxer, knocking the man back against the wall on the landing.

"Just stop!" Ballistic yells and keeps running, only to trade places with Trickster on the landing below. "Fuck!"

"You should know by now!" Trickster yells. "I'm nothing if not stubborn, Luke."

Ballistic pulls out a fishing weight. Conscious of his quickly dwindling supply, he takes a measured shot. Aiming it for the railing of the landing above him and letting it charge.

Trickster feels the impact before the floor beneath him gives away. Lurching forward as he's rocked by the impact. His arms flail, looking for something to hold onto as he curses. He looks around for the nearest mannequin to swap with as landing gives way. Popping in on the third floor landing, two stories below Ballistic as he looks to see the man jump over the gap he made.

Trickster curses to himselef as he climbs the stairs, the mannequins in sight all too damaged to swap with in an effective amount of time as Ballistic had taken to destroying any he sees on his way up. Making the difference in mass too great for a timely swap.

Finally making it to the roof. Ballistic slams the roof access door shut and pulls a small projectile from his pocket. Aiming it down, he fires one off and breaks the door handle. Taking a step back, he waits for moment. Upon hearing Francis slam into the door, he turns away.

"Luke! Don't do this!" Francis shouts, banging on the door furiously. "Please! Just walk away! Please! I'm literally begging you!"

"Just stay there!" Luke tells his former friend. "I'll do what we should've done a long time ago."

Ballistic turns to Noelle as she fights Genesis's construct. And pulls out an iron ball. Weighing roughly three pounds, it's not something he ever thought he'd use against anything living. He usually reserves it for breaking vehicles or even small buildings.

'Guess this is it.' He thinks to himself as Noelle, the creature, is only a building away. Too close to miss her body in the casing he knows she's held in.

He holds his arm out, uncaring of any harm that'll come to Trickster from being so close to the shot. Knowing thay whatever damage it is, he'll live.

He's tricky like that.

Ballistic closes his eyes as the energy charges up. Already at the point of no return, anything hit with the ball will break. At this point, he's sure he could take off Behemoth's head.

He's so focused on the fight that he fails to notice Trickster had managed to use a knife to jimmy the door open. And spotted Ballistic with a veritable missile in his hand, he runs up behind him.

Fueled by a feverish panic, he doesn't think. Just runs.

"Stop!" Trickster tackles Ballistic, knocking him over.

And making him unleash the projectile.

Right into the roof they're standing on.

Kakaaaaaak

The sound barrier breaks for the second time that night. And with it, the building. Sending Trickster and Ballistic falling faster than either can react.

With a sickening crunch, Ballistic and Trickster land in the small crater. Piled on top of the debris and rubble.

And all goes black.

…

…

…

Ballistic is the first recover consciousness. Pain wracking nearly every inch of his body as he tries to push up. Only to hiss in pain as he recognizes the sharp, throbbing pain in his chest and limbs. A pain he unfortunately knows too well.

Looking down, he sees his arm bent in two places. And he can feel the pain in his gut telling him he needs help now.

"Fuck." He pants out with a labored breath. Even breathing hurts his chest like blunt knives cutting him from the inside.

He tries to get up, the memory of what happened rushing back to him as he knows staying here would almost certainly get him killed. Whether it be something coming to kill him, or his own body hiving out. But the more he tries, the more his body protest.

'This is it.' He goes limp. 'I… always knew it'd end like this. Dead in the rubble of a fight I could've avoided… I just never imagined, it'd be a fight I got myself into.'

Defeated and done, he lets himself fall back. The sounds of fighting slowly reaching his ears.

'I'm going to die here.' He thinks to himself as he closes his eyes and lets his head fall to the side. 'This is it. I'm going to die, and it's all because I came back. Why? Why didn't I just leave?'

His mind can't come up with an answer. Leaving him to the silence of the broken building as he closes his eyes.

…

"Ugh." A single groan catches his attention.

Slowly cracking opening his eyes, Ballistic looks around for the noise. Remembering he wasn't the only one to fall, but surely Trickster teleported. Right?

And that's when his eyes spot it. His heart thudding him wide awake and with agonizing clarity as he sees Trickster, Francis. Not ten feet to his left, lower half crushed under rubble. A bent piece of rebar nailing him to the ground through his gut. The rusted metal having slipped under the bullet proof plate on hidden in his vest.

"No." Ballistic mutters softly. Not wanting to believe what he sees. Urging his body to move against all logic telling him to stay still.

Biting his lip to stifle the hiss of pain that threatens to escape. Luke slowly gets to his feet. And immediately regrets doing so as the dull pain in his gut becomes sharp and stabbing. Hunching over from the agony, Luke holds his stomach with his good arm.

Hobbling over to Francis, the ten feet feeling like an agonizing march under the weight of his injuries. Luke nearly collapses next to his former friend as he kneels down. Half sitting up, half leaning against a piece of the roof that fell next to him.

"Francis?" He says softly, but gets no response other than a sputtering and shaky breath. Concern for the man he went through so much with.

The mask on his face, cracked and chip, falls apart as he turns his head to look him in the eye. A single, teary eye staring almost vacantly at the armored mask Ballistic wears.

"Hey, hey say something." Luke says, hurriedly taking off his helmet and meeting Francis's eye. "Don't just sit there and stare!" Luke groans in pain under the effort of speaking. "Come on!"

He may not have liked Francis. But he didn't hate him. And on a certain level, he always understood him. Understood why he would do what he did.

It's why he never really blamed him.

Francis stares at him. But he can't hear him, the force of the sonic boom from earlier had blown his eardrums. Leaving him deaf to the world around him. As Ballistic talks, a dull ringing is all his ears pick up. And a tear rolls down his cheek as he feels himself grow cold.

Confused and scared. He utters a single sentence.

"A-am I… dying?" He croaks out. His voice barely above a whisper. "I… I don't… want…"

His arm twitches, moving up as though trying to reach for something. But it fails to move more than an inch as he lets out a strained breath. The light leaves his eyes, and a final tear falls from his dull eye as he goes limp. The rest of the mask falling away as Luke struggles to think.

"Damn it." Luke whispers hoarsely through the lump in his throat. Staring into the vacant eyes of Francis. "I told you to stop staring. Just stop staring already, damn it."

Luke reaches a shaky hand out, and drags it down over the corpse's face. Closing his eyes for the last time.

"Damn you." Luke says as he slowly lays down in the rubble. Whatever cruel or merciful force that was giving him the energy to move, quickly fading from his body as he stares up at the clear sky. The moon just in view as he closes his eyes.

"Damn it all."

-Time: 1:43am-

-West Slums, Tuesday, October 19th, 1:30am-

.

.

3rd Person POV, With Gully and Pinky

.

Pinky and Gully arrived to the scene of destruction with the help of Nightcrawler. The blue devil looking man having popped them across the city and into an alleyway a safe distance from the monster fight as they take in the sight. And can only balk at the ongoing destruction.

"Mein Gott." Nightcrawler shudders as he runs a hand through his short, curly black hair. "What is this? Is this an Endbringer?"

"No." Gully says as she looks over his shoulder to Echidna fighting the four armed black squid like monster. "Or at least, not any of the ones on record."

"I don't think we're cut out for this." Pinky says nervously as they step back and out of sight. "Like, I feel like Vicky or even Neil would be better suited to help."

"Why haven't they-" Nightcrawler goes to say something, but is cut off as a high pitched ting rings out. And he goes flying back.

"Nightcrawler!" Pinky shouts in distress as she runs to her friend sprawled out on the pavement, only for the same to happen to her. Her legs being taken out from under her and as a bone is definitely fractured from the hit. "Ah!"

"Pinky!" Gully throws herself over her friend and fellow hero. Just in time to receive a hit to her head from a metal object. One that burns.

"Hot dayum." She hears a man curse in front of her.

Looking up, Gully recognizes her assailant. He may be in a different suit, a bit color swapped, but she's seen him enough to recognize the Blue Blur of Brockton. Holding up a dented metal bat.

"A-Train?" Gully mutters in disbelief. And is met with a harsh swing to the head for her assumption.

"Don't compare me to that failure." He spits out with pure vitriol. "You're looking at Prime Time baby! Ain't no comparing me to anything else out there."

Confused and now sporting a headache. Gully moves to stand up, only to have her face beaten back by a highspeed swing of the bat. One that splits the skin of her forehead and cracks her nose.

"Agh!" She groans, holding her nose in pain. Feeling a little bloody trickle down her face and coat her hands.

"Damn, you're hard as a rock." Prime Time mutters as he looks to the bat, now dented and bent at an odd angle. "Wonder how much that holds up?" He looks to her with an unsettling grin.

Pinky remained quiet throughout the exchange. Silently enduring the pain in her legs while trying to think of what to do. Before it dawns on her as Prime Time disappears and comes back with another bat.

Pinky starts focusing, building up a basic fluid. Basic as in PH balance. Basing it in oils and giving it a hydrophobic property. Pinky keeps this in her and waits as Gully raises her arms to defend against the onslaught.

An unlucky swing from Prime Time manages to nail Gully's hand at just the right angle for her to snap her wrist and grab the offending weapon. Hissing under the heat it has built up. Gully punches the ground with her free hand, turning the flat surface into an uneven and rugged surface. Causing Prime Time to lose his balance.

"Whoa shit!" He curses under the force of the tremor. Stumbling slightly as he holds onto the bat for support while Pinky throws a hand out and a stream of slick oil coats the uneven ground.

Gully turns the ground flat again and pulls the bat. Making Prime Time fall over as the slick oil slips finds its way under his feet and stealing his stability. Falling right into Gully's open hand. She grabs him by the neck and stands up. Her enhanced strength and six foot and a half frame lifting the clone off his feet.

"You… have a lot of explaining to do." She huffs, feeling the heat radiate off of him through her hand and skin.

"Aghk! I ain't gotta do, shit!" He chokes out, grabbing her wrist with both hands. And delivering a high speed Indian burn.

"Ah!" Gully shouts in pain, dropping the man to hold her wrist and try to soothe the pain.

Prime Time turns to run away, nearly slipping and eating the pavement in his rush. Abandoning the trio for now as he retreats to rethink his approach. Having targeted and come up short twice in one night.

Pinky crawls out from underneath Gully as the large girl stands up. Getting to her hands and knees, Pinky pulls up her leggings and inspects her legs. Wincing at the two dark and angry bruises forming on her shins.

"Are you alright?" Gully asks, reaching out a hand to help her up.

"I don't think anything's broken." Pinky recoils slightly as weight is put on her legs. But aside from the soreness, she feels otherwise fine. "I think I'll be good for now."

"That's-" Gully starts.

"Night!" Pinky suddenly turns to the fallen mercenary. Jogging over and kneeling beside the bloodied man.

'Fine enough to jog.' Gully mentally notes.

Pinky goes to her secret friend and looks him over. Turning him from his back to his side like she remembered from some first aid class. Though she can't recall if it was specific to seizures or not.

Nightcrawler is unconscious, but breathing. His nose broken and bloody, along with several teeth having been knocked out.

"We-we need to get him out of here!" Pinky says with a tone of urgency, just as a loud crash is heard nearby.

"We can't." Gully says. "If he's hurt really bad then moving him too much might kill him."

"He was knocked in the teeth." Pinky hisses. "It's not like he was hit by a car!"

"Pinky!" Gully raises her voice. "He took a metal bat to the face. He could have a fractured vertebrae in his neck."

"Well then what are we-" Pinky starts, before the building next to them shakes and the two instinctively look up as debris falls around them.

Their eyes widen in horror as they see the silhouette of a large, arachnid squid like monster against the night sky. Panic and fear filling them and fueling their actions, Pinky turns to run.

But Gully stomps her foot and brings the earth around them to raise up and shield them. The sound of large cracks and the impact of stone on stone as the makeshift tent of earth protects them.

"What do we do!?" Pinky shouts over the sound of falling rubble.

"I-I, give me a minute!" Gully shouts as she tries to think. "We, we uh, we need to find a safer vantage point!"

"How?" Pinky asks just as the building above stops collapsing onto them. "And we can't leave Nightcrawler here, he'll die!"

"We, we need to. Um." Gully goes through the options in her head.

She never imagined she'd be in this situation. Where she'd be responsible for coordinating a response to an Endbringer event. She's not, but in the moment it feels that way. With a giant, now two giant monsters fighting a building away. A downed hero, and backup not guaranteed.

"Okay, we need to see who's here." Gully says as she pulls out her phone and accesses the tracker app to see where all the registered individuals are.

Dragon is registered as being on the other side of the building they're behind and across the street. Armsmaster is with her in roughly the same location. Firebreather and Laserdream are a few blocks away and moving towards them. Then there's Dauntless's signature not far away. There's also an unknown signature near that just reads new user. And Jenny is, nowhere near.

Zooming out of the map, Gully feels a pit form in her chest as she notices Jenny's signature is rapidly leaving the area.

She has no time to contemplate that though, as another rumble shakes the ground and the building next to them collapses. Falling on top of them as Echidna's weight smashes through the protective tent Gully made.

-Time 1:40am-

.

-West Slums, 1:35 am-

.
